failureNote: The question asks about cancellation, refund and remaining billing-period access. Some strategies retrieve the cancellation/refund docs but do not surface billing-period-access early enough.

strategyFindings.finding: TF-IDF ranked cancel-plan and refund-policy in the top 2 but missed billing-period-access in the top 5.
MiniLM ranked cancel-plan first and refund-policy third but billing-period-access appeared only at rank 4.
MPNet retrieved cancel-plan, refund-policy and billing-period-access in the top 3.

retrievalNote: Questions with multiple valid sources can look successful by Hit@1 while still missing supporting coverage. Recall@k is needed to catch this.

failureNote: The question asks about a failed card payment and workspace impact. The primary failed-payment source is easy to retrieve but supporting access-period context can be missed.

strategyFindings.finding: TF-IDF ranked failed-payment first but found billing-period-access only at rank 4.
MiniLM retrieved failed-payment and billing-period-access in the top 3.
MPNet ranked failed-payment first but missed billing-period-access in the top 5.

retrievalNote: A strategy can retrieve the primary source correctly while still missing an important supporting source. This is a source coverage issue not a complete retrieval failure.

failureNote: The question mixes invoice/payment wording with workspace access intent. The correct answer likely needs payment status, workspace access and entitlement sync sources but retrieval strategies are pulled toward different parts of the query.

strategyFindings.finding: TF-IDF ranked download-invoices and invite-team-members before the expected access and entitlement sources. It overweighted literal terms like invoice and team.
MiniLM also failed at rank 1 and ranked invite-team-members first. It captured team/workspace semantics but still missed the payment/access intent.
MPNet improved the result by ranking workspace-access first and entitlement-sync in the top 3 but it still missed failed-payment in the top 5.

retrievalNote: Multi-intent billing/access questions are difficult because different retrieval methods prioritize different parts of the query. This is a strong candidate for hybrid retrieval comparison.

failureNote: The question mentions an old billing admin leaving the company but the real task is updating the payment method, which belongs to billing permissions. Semantic retrieval can over-focus on the admin-left-company part.

strategyFindings.finding: TF-IDF ranked billing-permissions first, likely because the query contains billing and payment method terms.
MiniLM ranked change-admin-role first and billing-permissions second, showing semantic over-match on admin role language.
MPNet corrected this and ranked billing-permissions first.

retrievalNote: Semantic retrieval can over-focus on role/admin wording when the actual intent is billing permission. Stronger embedding models may handle this better but the result still depends on source wording.

failureNote: The question asks why paid features remain available after cancellation. The expected sources are cancellation and end-of-period access but keyword retrieval can be distracted by generic billing/refund/payment wording.

strategyFindings.finding: TF-IDF ranked refund-policy first, then cancel-plan, and only found billing-period-access at rank 5. It matched billing-like words but missed the access-after-cancellation rule.
MiniLM fixed the case by ranking billing-period-access first and cancel-plan second.
MPNet also fixed the case, ranking cancel-plan first and billing-period-access second.

retrievalNote: Embedding retrieval can improve semantic matching when the query describes a product rule indirectly such as continued access after cancellation.

failureNote: The question asks whether failed payment and cancellation are the same thing. The expected docs are failed-payment and cancel-plan but some strategies over-rank adjacent billing/access docs.

strategyFindings.finding: TF-IDF ranked failed-payment first but missed cancel-plan in the top 5.
MiniLM ranked billing-period-access first then retrieved failed-payment and cancel-plan at ranks 2 and 3.
MPNet retrieved failed-payment and cancel-plan at ranks 1 and 2.

retrievalNote: Comparison-style questions need both contrasted sources. Semantic retrieval may surface a related access doc first, while keyword retrieval may retrieve one side of the comparison and miss the other.

failureNote: The question combines upgrade, project limits and export limits. The expected docs are upgrade-plan and plan-limits but export-related terms can pull retrieval toward export docs.

strategyFindings.finding: TF-IDF ranked upgrade-plan first but pushed plan-limits to rank 5 because export docs matched the export wording.
MiniLM improved the result by ranking plan-limits first and upgrade-plan second.
MPNet also ranked plan-limits first and upgrade-plan second, keeping both expected sources in the top 3.

retrievalNote: Embedding retrieval can improve source coverage for multi-topic queries when the query combines limits, upgrade intent and product capacity language.

failureNote: The question combines invoice management with a missing export button. The expected docs are export-permissions and billing-permissions but retrieval tends to focus on export-related docs and push billing-permissions down.

strategyFindings.finding: TF-IDF ranked export-permissions first and found billing-permissions at rank 5, giving weak early source coverage.
MiniLM ranked export-permissions first but missed billing-permissions in the top 5.
MPNet ranked export-permissions first and found billing-permissions at rank 5, similar to TF-IDF.

retrievalNote: Permission-scope questions may require clearer source wording because both keyword and embedding retrieval can focus on the dominant action such as export, while missing the secondary permission source.
